summary: Knorr-Bremse AG is the parent company of a global market leader in braking systems for rail and commercial vehicles, generating EUR 7.8 billion in sales in 2025. The company faces legal risks including a 2018 U.S. Department of Justice antitrust complaint over alleged unlawful no-poach agreements with a competitor. Additionally, a dispute among the heirs of former chief Heinz Hermann Thiele over his estate introduces moderate legal risk, while a Supervisory Board finding in 2025 determined Julia Thiele-Schürhoff is not independent due to her interest in the controlling shareholder.

risk_flags.title: 2018 U.S. Antitrust Complaint on No-Poach Agreements
risk_flags.finding: In April 2018, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a civil antitrust complaint alleging Knorr-Bremse AG and Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation entered into unlawful no-poach agreements. The complaint alleged that Knorr Brake Company instructed outside recruiters not to solicit from Wabtec, and that the agreement was known to senior executives at the parent companies, including top Knorr executives in Germany.

risk_flags.title: Dispute Over Thiele Estate
risk_flags.finding: The heirs of former Knorr-Bremse chief Heinz Hermann Thiele remain in a dispute over his multi-billion estate, with his son, widow and the executor litigating against each other.

risk_flags.title: Supervisory Board Independence Finding
risk_flags.finding: In December 2025, the Supervisory Board judged Julia Thiele-Schürhoff not independent because of her indirect interest in the controlling shareholder KB Holding GmbH.

risk_flags.title: Company Registration
risk_flags.finding: Knorr-Bremse AG is registered at the District Court of Munich under HRB 42031.

risk_flags.title: Group Structure and Market Position
risk_flags.finding: Knorr-Bremse AG acts as the parent company of the Group's two corporate divisions and all regional companies, describing itself as the global market and technology leader for braking systems. The Group generated sales of approximately EUR 7.8 billion in 2025.

risk_flags.title: Rail Vehicle Braking System Patents
risk_flags.finding: Knorr-Bremse Systeme für Schienenfahrzeuge GmbH filed patent applications for a control apparatus for a braking device and for control of rail vehicle parameters, and holds a granted German patent for a braking system for a rail vehicle and a method for controlling it.

claims.quote: Today the Knorr-Bremse Group, based in Munich, is the global market and technology leader for braking systems and a leading supplier of other innovative solutions for the rail and commercial vehicle industries.

claims.statement: The U.S. Department of Justice filed a civil antitrust Complaint on 3 April 2018 alleging that Knorr-Bremse AG and Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation entered into unlawful no-poach agreements in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act.
claims.quote: On April 3, 2018, the United States filed a Complaint alleging that Knorr-Bremse AG (“Knorr”) and Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation (“Wabtec”) entered into unlawful agreements not to poach employees in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. 1.

claims.statement: The DOJ Complaint alleged that Knorr Brake Company, in furtherance of the no-poach agreement, instructed outside recruiters not to solicit employees from Wabtec.
claims.quote: The Complaint further alleges that in furtherance of their agreement, Wabtec and Knorr Brake Company informed their outside recruiters not to solicit employees from the other company.

claims.statement: The DOJ Complaint alleged that the no-poach agreement was known to senior executives at the parent companies, including top Knorr executives in Germany.
claims.quote: that agreement was well-known to senior executives at the parent companies, including top Knorr executives in Germany who were included in key communications about the No-Poach Agreement.

claims.statement: NTSB highway accident investigation of a motorcoach equipped with Knorr-Bremse (Bendix) type SN7 air disc brakes found the air brake system functional and undamaged, with rotors and pads within specified wear limits; vehicle mechanical defects were not a factor in the accident.
claims.quote: The air brake system was examined and found to be functional and undamaged, passing all system checks; the brake disc rotors and pads were found to be within specified wear limits.
